The weakened invariant gives the verifier no such facts for the column n-1, so it cannot prove preservation in this form. It also breaks the bridge: at loop exit with n == b.Length, the clause n <= j+1 still holds for j = b.Length-1. Pairs in the last column of b are therefore never constrained, and the postcondition cannot be derived. Removing the +1 gives the standard canyon-search invariant. reasoning_content:
I'm examining whether the weakened invariant with the "+1" term actually still guarantees the loop's preservation and postcondition, since it seems to let the index go one step further than it should without being properly checked.

So the correct standard invariant should really be m<=i && n<=j, not j+1. Checking preservation confirms: when a[m]<=b[n], advancing m still satisfies d<=dist(m,j) for any j>=n since b[j]>=b[n]>=a[m]. This classifies as an invariant/preservation issue.
